title: Team Impedance Mapper and Stable Interface Contracts
creator: Priya Khanna
description:
Problem: When multiple teams (Eng, Design, Security, Infra) own adjacent surfaces for a shared initiative, we repeatedly encounter blocked handoffs, unclear interface expectations, and last-minute scope changes that cascade into release slippage. Existing dependency boards list blockers but do not articulate the implicit integration expectations (format, performance envelope, observability contract) that cause most rework.

Goal: Build a lightweight "Impedance Mapper" workflow and a canonical Stable Interface Contract (SIC) template to sit alongside Linear dependency tickets. The mapper will calculate an "impedance score" that combines scope volatility, API/contract maturity, historical handoff latency, and required infra change footprint. The SIC defines mandatory fields to reduce ambiguity (consumers, providers, data schema, latency SLO, rollout steps, rollback criteria, telemetry hooks, and security obligations).

Scope: Minimum viable outcome for this ticket is a productized process and tooling that: 1) attaches an SIC JSON blob to dependency tickets, 2) surfaces impedance scores in the roadmap view and in the weekly readiness board, and 3) wires a minimal alert when impedance > threshold (auto-escalate to program owner).

Out of scope: full automation of contract enforcement (that will be follow-up work), migration of historical tickets, and mandatory gating until pilot feedback is positive.

Why this matters: By making the expectations explicit up-front we reduce churn at handoff time, accelerate testing windows, and give PMs and EMs an objective signal to prioritize early integration work. The impedance score also helps sales/customer-facing teams set realistic delivery expectations for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: SIC template created and documented in Confluence with example for a runtime/console integration
Linear ticket UI has a field for attaching SIC JSON (or link) and displays impedance score
Impedance score calculation documented and validated with two past initiatives producing sensible scores
Weekly readiness board shows top-10 high-impedance dependencies and owners
Auto-escalation rule in PagerDuty/Slack when impedance > 8 and due_date within 3 sprints
tasks: Draft SIC schema and get design/eng/security sign-off
Prototype a scoring function using historical ticket metadata and manual weights
Add a custom field to Linear for SIC attachment and impedance numeric value
Create Confluence playbook + example contracts for: API-only, infra-change, and UX-change flows
Implement a weekly job to compute impedance and populate roadmap widget (PoC via BigQuery)
Set up Slack/PagerDuty escalation channel and runbook for >8 impedance alerts
Pilot with two active initiatives (one runtime infra change, one console UX change) for 6 weeks
comments: 2025-02-16 Priya Khanna: Kickoff with Eng/Design/Security. Agreed to aim for a lightweight JSON SIC rather than a heavy Confluence-only doc. Sec to propose mandatory fields for data classification.

2025-02-20 Miguel Ortega: Ran a preliminary scan of 18 past cross-team tickets; handoff latency correlates with absent schema and missing telemetry hooks. Draft scoring weights attached to the Confluence page: volatility=3, infra-impact=4, telemetry-gap=2, stakeholder-count=1.

2025-02-27 Aisha Patel (Design): Provided SIC UX examples for consumer/provider responsibilities and rollout checklist. Wants a short checklist card that lives in Linear so designers can sign-off earlier.

2025-03-01 Carlos Mendes (Security): Security fields added — data_classification, required_encryption, and threat_model_reference. Suggested a preflight security review flag when sensitive data is present.

2025-03-03 Miguel Ortega: Updated acceptance criteria to include two-pilot validation and added PagerDuty channel. Next: engineering spike to add Linear custom field and a BigQuery job for score calculation.
